question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_b: A hydraulic device used to raise the landing gear
choice_c: A specialized tool for testing air brake pressure
choice_d: A device used only for measuring kingpin height
explanation: The manual states a converter dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.1

question: Before backing a converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer's height?
choice_a: It must be the same height as the tractor frame
choice_b: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_c: It must be raised to its maximum height
choice_d: It doesn't matter as long as the brakes are locked
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to make sure trailer height is correct: slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When wheeling a converter dolly into position by hand, it should be lined up with what?
choice_a: The rear axle of the trailer
choice_b: The landing gear crank
choice_c: The kingpin
choice_d: The pintle hook of the tractor
explanation: The manual says to wheel the dolly into position by hand so it is in line with the kingpin.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

topic: Coupling converter dolly - securing before backing under
question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, what should you do regarding the trailer's brakes or wheels?
choice_a: Release the trailer brakes completely
choice_b: Disconnect the air lines
choice_c: Lower the landing gear fully
choice_d: Make sure trailer brakes are locked and/or wheels chocked
explanation: The manual states to make sure trailer brakes are locked and/or wheels chocked before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: How should you test the coupling between the converter dolly and the second (rear) semitrailer?
choice_a: Pull against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_b: Drive forward at normal highway speed
choice_c: Apply the trailer brakes hard while backing up
choice_d: Visually inspect from a distance without touching the rig
explanation: The manual directs drivers to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: What should a visual check of the coupling confirm?
choice_a: The trailer's lights are functioning
choice_b: There is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
choice_c: The tires are properly inflated
choice_d: The landing gear crank is greased
explanation: The manual specifies making a visual check of coupling: no space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on kingpin.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords when coupling the dolly to the second trailer, what should you do next?
choice_a: Open the air tank petcock fully and leave all valves open
choice_b: Remove the air tank from the dolly
choice_c: Close the converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer (service and emergency shut-offs)
choice_d: Disconnect the safety chains
explanation: The manual instructs to close the converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer after connecting the chains, hoses, and cords.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Checking air reaches the rear trailer
question: After charging the trailer brakes on a newly coupled double, how do you confirm air pressure reaches the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: Listen at the front of the tractor for hissing
choice_b: Check the fuel gauge reading
choice_c: Assume air pressure is fine if the engine is running
choice_d: Open the emergency line shut-off at the rear of the second trailer and check for air; if it isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work
explanation: The manual says to charge trailer brakes and check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Where should the rig be parked before uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles?
choice_a: In a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_b: On a slight downhill grade for easier separation
choice_c: With the front wheels turned sharply
choice_d: On loose gravel or sand
explanation: The manual's uncoupling procedure begins with parking the rig in a straight line on firm, level ground.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Before pulling the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer, what should you do with that trailer's landing gear?
choice_a: Fully raise the landing gear
choice_b: Lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly
choice_c: Remove the landing gear entirely
choice_d: Leave the landing gear exactly as it was during transport
explanation: The manual instructs lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly before uncoupling.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: What must be done before slowly pulling the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer?
choice_a: Increase tractor speed and pull sharply
choice_b: Fill the dolly's air tank completely and lock all brakes
choice_c: Close air shut-offs at the rear of the first semitrailer, disconnect and secure the dolly's air and electric lines, and release the dolly brakes and fifth wheel latch
choice_d: Remove the safety chains from the front trailer only
explanation: The manual lists these steps in order before pulling the dolly clear: close air shut-offs at the rear of the first semitrailer, disconnect all dolly air and electric lines and secure them, release dolly brakes, and release the converter dolly fifth wheel latch.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: What does the manual warn drivers never to do?
choice_a: Never grease the pintle hook before a trip
choice_b: Never lock the pintle hook before backing up
choice_c: Never inspect the pintle hook while the rig is parked
choice_d: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer
explanation: The manual explicitly warns to never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

topic: Why the pintle hook warning matters
question: Why does the manual warn against unlocking the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: It will immediately drain all air from the brake system
choice_c: It voids the vehicle's warranty
choice_d: It causes the trailer's electrical system to short out
explanation: The manual explains that unlocking the pintle hook with the dolly still under the trailer may cause the dolly tow bar to fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: After pulling clear of the trailer, what should you do to secure the converter dolly during uncoupling?
choice_a: Leave the dolly's wheels completely free to roll
choice_b: Apply the converter gear spring brakes or chock the wheels
choice_c: Remove the dolly's wheels for inspection
choice_d: Disconnect the landing gear entirely
explanation: The manual instructs applying the converter gear spring brakes or chocking the wheels when uncoupling the dolly.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: What is the correct sequence for coupling a triple-trailer rig, according to the manual?
choice_a: Couple all three trailers to the dolly simultaneously
choice_b: Couple the third (rearmost) trailer first, then work forward
choice_c: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the same method as coupling doubles
choice_d: Couple the two dollies together before attaching any trailer
explanation: The manual describes coupling the tractor to the first trailer, then using the converter dolly to couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles, completing the triples rig.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is uncoupled first?
choice_a: The first (front) trailer
choice_b: The middle trailer
choice_c: All three trailers at the same time
choice_d: The third (rearmost) trailer, by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it using the method for uncoupling doubles
explanation: The manual states to uncouple the third trailer first by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Uncouple Triple-trailer Rig

question: For coupling and uncoupling truck-trailer combinations not specifically described in the manual, what does it advise drivers to do?
choice_a: Learn the correct way to couple and uncouple the vehicle(s) according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications
choice_b: Always use the standard doubles method regardless of the combination
choice_c: Never attempt to couple combinations not described in the manual
choice_d: Contact the DMV before attempting any coupling
explanation: The manual notes there are too many combinations to cover and advises drivers to learn the correct method according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.4 Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: What inspection procedure does the manual say to use as the basis for inspecting a doubles/triples combination vehicle?
choice_a: A simplified two-step check unique to combination vehicles
choice_b: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_c: A checklist provided only by the vehicle manufacturer
choice_d: No formal inspection procedure is specified
explanation: The manual states to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect the combination vehicle, with additional items specific to doubles/triples.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3 Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel during a doubles/triples inspection, the locking jaws should be positioned around what part of the kingpin?
choice_a: The head of the kingpin
choice_b: Either the head or the shank, it doesn't matter
choice_c: The shank, not the head, of the kingpin
choice_d: The base plate of the fifth wheel only
explanation: The manual specifies checking that locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

topic: Fifth wheel positioned too far forward
question: What could happen if the fifth wheel is positioned too far forward?
choice_a: The trailer's electrical system will fail
choice_b: The air brakes will automatically release
choice_c: The kingpin will disconnect while driving straight
choice_d: The tractor frame could hit the landing gear, or the cab could hit the trailer, during turns
explanation: The manual warns to check that the fifth wheel is not so far forward that the tractor frame will hit the landing gear, or the cab will hit the trailer, during turns.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

question: For a set of double or triple trailers, what is the correct position of the shut-off valves at the rear of the front trailer(s) compared to the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Rear of front trailers: OPEN; rear of last trailer: CLOSED
choice_b: Rear of front trailers: CLOSED; rear of last trailer: OPEN
choice_c: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be OPEN
choice_d: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be CLOSED
explanation: The manual specifies: rear of front trailers OPEN, rear of last trailer CLOSED.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

topic: Converter dolly air tank drain valve
question: During inspection, what should the converter dolly air tank drain valve be set to?
choice_a: Open
choice_b: Closed
choice_c: Half open, to allow moisture to drain
choice_d: Removed entirely
explanation: The manual lists the converter dolly air tank drain valve as CLOSED among the additional inspection checks.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks

topic: Checking air flows to all trailers
question: During the 'Check That Air Flows to All Trailers' test, after opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer, what confirms the entire system is charged?
choice_a: The dashboard warning light turning off
choice_b: A rise in engine RPM
choice_c: Hearing air escaping at the rear, showing the entire system is charged
choice_d: The parking brake releasing automatically
explanation: The manual states you should hear air escaping when opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer, showing the entire system is charged.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks

question: During the Test Tractor Protection Valve check, the trailer air supply control should pop out (go to emergency) within about what air pressure range, per the manufacturer's specification?
choice_a: 5 to 10 psi
choice_b: 60 to 80 psi
choice_c: 100 to 120 psi
choice_d: 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The manual states this usually occurs within the range of 20 to 45 psi, as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Test Tractor Protection Valve

topic: Consequence of a failed tractor protection valve
question: What could happen if the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly?
choice_a: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control
choice_b: The trailer's turn signals would stop working
choice_c: The fifth wheel would automatically unlock
choice_d: Fuel consumption would increase noticeably
explanation: The manual explains that if the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: How should you test the trailer service brakes according to the manual?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake and check for any vehicle movement
choice_b: With normal air pressure, release the parking brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly, and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) to feel them come on
choice_c: Disconnect the emergency line and listen for escaping air
choice_d: Check tire pressure at each trailer wheel
explanation: The manual instructs checking for normal air pressure, releasing the parking brakes, moving forward slowly, and applying trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) to feel that they are connected and working.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Test Trailer Service Brakes
